messages:
Eli: Hey folks, just unboxed my MacBook Pro and during setup it asked for my Apple ID and I used my personal one. Now the machine says it's "activated" but the MDM never finished and System Settings shows no profiles. OOBE says 'This Mac appears to be registered to a different organization' when I try to sign in with company SSO. What did I break?
Jordan (IT): Welcome Eli! That happens when personal Apple ID/Activation Lock interferes with Automated Device Enrollment (DEP). Can you paste the serial (run `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep Serial`)? We'll check the DEP/Apple Business Manager record.
Eli: Serial: C02GHT9876LK. I still have the box and the receipt if that helps.
MDM-Bot: Device C02GHT9876LK: DEP record found (assigned to Redwood Inference), status: awaiting-user-activation. Last contact: 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z (no MDM check-in). Activation Lock: personal Apple ID detected.
Jordan (IT): Yep — Activation Lock tied to the personal Apple ID is blocking the automated enrollment. Two routes: 1) If you're near an Apple Store we can ask them to remove Activation Lock with proof of purchase (takes a bit), 2) We can schedule an on-site reimage where IT will use Apple Configurator (requires a host Mac and a USB-C cable) to revive and supervise the device so it enrolls correctly. Which is feasible for you?
Eli: I'm remote and don't have another Mac. Shipping it back is ok but prefer to avoid returns if possible. Is there a self-service fix?
Shipping: If you still have the original reseller invoice and the serial on the box, we can start an Activation Lock removal request with Apple Business Manager, but it usually takes 24–72 hours. We can fast-track if you need it urgently.
Jordan (IT): Also quick note: if you still have access to the personal Apple ID used during setup, you can sign in at icloud.com/find, select the device, and remove it from the account (turn off Activation Lock). That would immediately allow DEP to proceed. Do you remember the Apple ID creds?
Eli: I do remember them. I'll log in and try to remove the device now.
Eli: OK I signed into iCloud, found the Mac under Devices, removed it from my account. It shows as removed.
MDM-Bot: DEP record re-evaluated: Activation Lock cleared for C02GHT9876LK. Enrollment push queued.
Jordan (IT): Great — reboot and you should see the MDM enrollment prompt during Setup Assistant. If it still hangs, run `sudo profiles show --all` after you finish setup and paste output.
Eli: Rebooted and now I got the company welcome screen and SSO prompt. Completed SSO and accepted the configuration profile. It shows profile: corp-managed-mac.
Jordan (IT): Perfect. Confirm FileVault is enabled: System Settings > Privacy & Security > FileVault. We require it ON; the key will be escrowed automatically. Also run `profiles status -type enrollment` to confirm check-in.
Eli: FileVault: On (escrowed). `profiles status -type enrollment` output: 'MDM enrolled (corp-managed-mac), last-checkin: 2026-06-15T10:02:12Z'.
MDM-Bot: Device C02GHT9876LK check-in: 2026-06-15T10:02:12Z. Profile applied: corp-managed-mac. Recovery key escrow: OK.
Jordan (IT): Closing loop: all good now. If you had installed anything under your personal account during the earlier step, we recommend wiping and reinstalling apps under the managed user to avoid policy conflicts. Logged ticket IT-5238 for the Activation Lock removal and enrollment.
Eli: Thanks team — sorry for the mess, and appreciate the clear steps. Saved the lesson: always skip Apple ID during OOBE for corporate devices :grimacing:
Ops: Quick FYI for new-hires: we added a line to the onboarding doc about avoiding personal Apple IDs during setup and steps to fix Activation Lock.
Eli: That's super helpful — thanks everyone :rocket:
